document_title: Where Are the 3,048? The Map Alaska Hasn't Drawn
post_copy:
If a state letter about your citizenship came and you set it aside, your registration stays inactive.

The machine here was two lists. Elections asked the DMV to compare them in March 2026.
Jeannie McLeod, 75, of Anchorage legally changed her first name when she naturalized in 2024.

The check usually returns about 200 names. This time 3,048 registrations were moved to inactive.
She says she was put back on the rolls under "a name that is not legally mine."

Rep. Kevin McCabe says this is the division's job. The state's answer is a questioned ballot.

The comparison ran in bulk. The proof runs one at a time.

The state's three counts, what the letter asks of you, the pushback, the defense, and the map of the 3,048 nobody has drawn.

Before Alaska gives AI more authority, does the flag get the benefit of the doubt, or does the person?

#AlaskaElections #VoterRolls #AIGovernance
first_comment:
Sources for today's deck, in the order the claims appear.

Alaska Public Media, July 23, 2026, on the Division of Elections moving voters to inactive status after a DMV list comparison, including Director Carol Beecher's "probably very old data" and what a flagged voter must do next.
https://alaskapublic.org/news/2026-07-23/state-removes-3-500-alaskans-from-voter-rolls-based-in-part-on-old-data

KMXT and Alaska Public Media, July 30, 2026, Liz Ruskin, on the bipartisan letter asking for the names back, and on Jeannie McLeod of Anchorage.
https://www.kmxt.org/alaska-statewide-news/2026-07-30/23-alaska-legislators-ask-state-to-restore-voters-wrongfully-removed-from-the-rolls

Alaska's News Source, July 29, 2026, Wil Courtney, carrying the joint Division of Elections and DMV statement and the letter's own words.
https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/07/30/lawmakers-say-elections-division-illegally-deactivated-registration-thousands-voters-urges-director-reverse-decision/

U.S. Department of the Air Force, April 10, 2026, on roughly 4,700 acres across twelve parcels at JBER, Eielson and Clear offered for AI data centers. Background, outside this story's window.
https://www.af.mil/News/Article-Display/Article/4456660/daf-takes-steps-for-potential-alaskan-ai-data-centers/

Office of the Lieutenant Governor of Alaska, for the August 18, 2026 primary date.
https://ltgov.alaska.gov/newsroom/2026/06/lt-governor-nancy-dahlstrom-opens-investigation-to-determine-validity-of-dan-j-sullivan-filing-for-u-s-senate/

Two things this deck deliberately does not say. It doesn't say the deactivation was illegal, because that is the legislators' allegation and no statute text was reachable to test it. And it doesn't say nobody reviewed the flags, because no published account describes a human check either way. Absence of a description is not evidence of absence.

aftercare: Post Tuesday to Thursday, 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time. The August 18 primary makes this deck time-sensitive; it loses most of its value after that date.
Paste the first comment immediately, within about 60 seconds of posting.
Reply substantively to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes.
If someone asks whether this was AI, the answer is no, and that is the deck's point. It was a comparison of two lists.
If someone says the deactivation was illegal, note that this is what the legislators' letter alleges and that no court has ruled.
